# SSH-013: Home, ~/.ssh and authorized_keys are not writable by others

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

Anyone who can write to a user's home, ~/.ssh or authorized_keys can add their own key and log in as that user. sshd's StrictModes also refuses keys in that state, which can lock the user out. A ~/.ssh directory that is not 0700 is a warning.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ls -ld ~USER ~USER/.ssh ~USER/.ssh/authorized_keys
```

## How to fix it

chmod go-w ~USER; chmod 700 ~USER/.ssh; chmod 600 ~USER/.ssh/authorized_keys; chown the files to the user.

Run `stackward explain SSH-013` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
